description: A grant is a funding award offered by a government agency, foundation, or other funder that eligible applicants can apply for to support a specific project, program, or research; it excludes sample proposals, how-to guides, news articles about awarded grants, and funder profile pages.
confusables: news articles about previously awarded grants
grant outcome reports or white papers
loans, contracts, or other non-grant funding instruments
examples: Rural Community Development Block Grant — 2024 Cycle
Climate Action Innovation Fund — Small Grants for Nonprofits

fields.name: title
fields.description: The official name of the grant program as displayed at the top of the grant's detail page.
fields.example: Rural Community Development Block Grant — 2024 Cycle

fields.name: funder
fields.description: The organization, agency, or foundation offering the grant, usually shown as a logo with name near the top.

fields.name: summary
fields.description: A short paragraph describing the grant's purpose and what it funds.
fields.example: Provides funding to support community infrastructure, housing, and economic development projects in rural areas.

fields.name: amount
fields.description: The award ceiling or range, usually displayed with a dollar sign and sometimes 'up to' or 'between'; commonly formatted like $50,000 or $25,000–$250,000.

fields.name: application_deadline
fields.description: The date by which applications must be submitted, usually labeled 'Deadline' or 'Application Due Date'.

fields.name: posted_date
fields.description: The date the grant opportunity was posted or opened, typically labeled 'Posted' or 'Open Date'.

fields.name: eligibility
fields.description: Description of who can apply (e.g., nonprofits, states, individuals), usually in a dedicated 'Eligibility' section.
fields.example: State, local, and tribal governments; nonprofit organizations with 501(c)(3) status

fields.name: grant_id
fields.description: An identifier assigned by the funder (e.g., an Opportunity Number on Grants.gov or a foundation reference code); often near the title.

fields.name: application_url
fields.description: Direct link to the application portal, instructions, or downloadable application package (PDF/Word).

fields.name: categories
fields.description: Topic tags or categories assigned to the grant (e.g., 'Education', 'Environment'), usually shown as chips or a comma-separated list.
